newsitem.title: USA: Sinatra could leave hospital this week - publicist.
newsitem.headline: Sinatra could leave hospital this week - publicist.

text.p: Frank Sinatra, who was rushed to the hospital last Thursday after suffering a heart attack, is undergoing "appropriate treatment" and could be released later this week, his publicist said on Tuesday.
"His prognosis is still good and his doctors say hopefully he can go home sometime later this week," said Susan Reynolds.

The 81-year-old singer and movie star was in a private room at Cedars-Sinai Medical Centre, where he was admitted last Thursday after suffering what his doctors called an "uncomplicated heart attack."
Reynolds said Sinatra was undergoing "appropriate treatment," but she declined to say what that was.

Soon after Sinatra entered the hospital, NBC News cited unnamed sources saying he was suffering from Alzheimer's disease, a degenerative brain disorder. But Reynolds and Sinatra's family members have steadfastly denied the report.
Sinatra was rushed back to Cedars-Sinai only two days after being released from the hospital, where he spent Monday night last week with an undisclosed complaint.

In November, he spent eight days at the same hospital after being admitted for what was described as a pinched nerve. He later developed pneumonia and was also reported to have suffered a minor heart attack at the time.
